commits.message:
Demo: substantially upgrade system-map diagram

Promote the system map from a thin top strip to a proper architectural
diagram drawn as a single SVG with viewBox 0 0 1200 280. Communicates
four facts at a glance:

  1. cherry's centrality (gradient fill, purple emphasis, soft halo
     behind it).
  2. one MCP surface in, two protocol surfaces out (three labeled
     branches with named transports).
  3. renderer + main are halves of *one* Electron OS process (drawn as
     a dashed-border container around both).
  4. the actual wires (CDP `wss://localhost:9222`, V8 `ws://localhost:
     9229`, MCP `JSON-RPC over stdio`).

Nodes render as rounded SVG rects with linear-gradient fills, icons
(◇ / 🍒 / ◈), title + monospace sub-text. Cherry gets a larger size,
purple stroke, drop-shadow glow, and a radial halo behind it. Connection
arrows are cubic bezier curves with derived arrowheads (parsed from the
path's d-string so the head sits exactly at the path end). Each
connection has a centered protocol label.

Flash mechanism unchanged — overlay paths run @keyframes ec-arrow-flash
on traffic — but they now paint over a meaningful diagram instead of
abstract arrows.

Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.ai/code)
via [Happy](https://happy.engineering)

Co-Authored-By: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>
Co-Authored-By: Happy <yesreply@happy.engineering>

Demo: replace particles with system-map topology diagram

Original vanilla-JS demo had a persistent routing diagram in its center
column — labeled nodes connected by SVG arrows that flashed the
protocol's color when traffic crossed them. The previous particle-arc
attempts kept missing the point: what's informative is the *system
map*, not the motion.

Port that pattern to the React showcase as a top-of-stage strip:

    [ agent ]  --MCP-->  [ 🍒 cherry ]  --CDP-->  [ renderer ]
                                       \\--V8 -->  [ main ]

Five labeled nodes, three branched arrows. Arrows are always visible at
neutral grey; when the orchestrator emits a flash for a connection,
an overlay path runs `@keyframes ec-arrow-flash` (stroke fades in to
the protocol's color with drop-shadow glow, then back out, 700ms) and
self-removes via timer. Multiple overlapping flashes layer naturally,
so an arrow reads as "sustained traffic" while a step's wire messages
are in flight.

ConnectionId is now 'agent-cherry' | 'cherry-cdp' | 'cherry-v8' — CDP
and V8 are separate branches off cherry, the way the original showed
them. Orchestrator emits 'agent-cherry'/mcp at tool-call begin and end,
'cherry-cdp'/cdp on each CDP wire round-trip, 'cherry-v8'/v8 likewise.
All previous flow-packet plumbing replaced (DataflowLayer.tsx removed,
state.flowPackets renamed to state.flashes with the new shape).

Hidden under 760px viewport (matches ScrollPin's mobile breakpoint;
strip would be cramped at phone widths and the actor panes already
stack).

Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.ai/code)
via [Happy](https://happy.engineering)

Co-Authored-By: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>
Co-Authored-By: Happy <yesreply@happy.engineering>

Demo: dataflow animation showing the three-actor protocol routing

During scripted scenarios, packets now arc between the agent, cherry,
and application panes in sequence — making the routing electric-cherry
performs visible at the wire level. Color = protocol so a glance tells
you whether the call rode CDP (blue) or V8 Inspector (orange); the
agent-cherry hops are magenta to distinguish MCP request/response from
the underlying protocol.

Sequence per scripted step:
  1. Agent issues tool call → packet from .ec-agent to .ec-cherry (mcp)
  2. Per CDP/V8 wire message: cherry ↔ application round-trip on that
     protocol, fired alongside the existing wire-log dispatches.
  3. Once the wire loop completes: packet from .ec-cherry to .ec-agent
     (mcp) — the response unwinding back to the agent.

Same data-as-state architecture as the earlier iteration: orchestrator
appends FlowPacket entries; each packet self-removes after its
animateMotion duration. Layer measures stage rect via ResizeObserver
and queries source/target selectors at packet-mount time so coordinates
stay correct across the scroll-pin lock-in.

Inspector modal sits at a higher z-index, so opening it hides any
in-flight particles — clean reading state.

Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.ai/code)
via [Happy](https://happy.engineering)

Co-Authored-By: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>
Co-Authored-By: Happy <yesreply@happy.engineering>

Extract MCP tool catalog; showcase reads it as single source of truth

Two coupled changes:

1. Move the inline `tools: Tool[]` array out of src/index.ts into a new
   src/tool-catalog.ts. The catalog file has zero runtime dependencies
   (locally-defined types, no SDK imports) so a browser bundle can
   import it as readily as the Node MCP server. Each entry now carries
   a `category` field so consumers can group without re-deriving the
   taxonomy from name patterns.

2. Replace the showcase demo's clickable-chip behavior. Old behavior
   pushed a synthetic round-trip through the wire log — informative
   only insofar as the chip felt alive. New behavior opens a modal
   "tool inspector" populated entirely from TOOL_CATALOG: description,
   typed parameter list with required/default/enum metadata, and an
   example call synthesized from the schema's required fields. The
   showcase no longer ships hand-written examples that drift; the
   inspector renders whatever the server's schema currently says.

   Showcase's data/tools.ts also derives palette grouping from the
   catalog's `category` field. The palette layout, group labels, and
   protocol routing per group are all generated from one pass through
   TOOL_CATALOG. The hardcoded TOOL_PALETTE / GROUP_LABEL /
   GROUP_PROTOCOL maps are gone — adding a tool to the catalog with a
   known category makes it appear in the palette automatically. Tool
   count in the palette header now derives from TOOL_CATALOG.length.

The dataflow particle layer is removed entirely (DataflowLayer.tsx
deleted, flowPackets state torn out of usePlayer). The user's feedback
was that the animation wasn't useful — info is. The palette now
behaves as an interactive reference card for the live MCP catalog.

Showcase tsconfig adds ../src/tool-catalog.ts to its include list, and
the Vite config opens server.fs.allow to '..' so the dev server can
read the catalog file. Production builds aren't restricted by fs.allow.

Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.ai/code)
via [Happy](https://happy.engineering)

Co-Authored-By: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>
Co-Authored-By: Happy <yesreply@happy.engineering>

Demo: clickable tool chips + dataflow particles between panels

Two related changes:

1. Tool chips in the palette are now buttons. Clicking one fires off a
   one-shot manual invocation: highlights the chip, emits a wire row
   round-trip on the chip's protocol (CDP or V8), and shows the same
   dataflow animation a scripted scenario does. Doesn't disrupt the
   running scenario — visitors get tactile feedback that the chips are
   real entry points and which protocol each routes to.

2. New `<DataflowLayer>` overlays the stage and animates SVG particles
   along curved paths between source/target rects (chip ↔ application
   pane) for every wire-message round-trip. Each particle is a row in
   `state.flowPackets` with `protocol` and source/target selectors —
   the orchestrator appends, the layer renders, each <Packet>
   self-removes via timer when its animateMotion completes. No
   choreography in user code; it's all driven by state.

Selectors live in the packet so the layer has no domain knowledge of
"which side does what" — only the orchestrator decides chip→app vs
app→chip per direction.

Add showcase/ Vite app + GitHub Pages deploy workflow

The previous gh-pages branch was experimentally hosting both Vite source
and the multiplexer's deploy outputs on the same branch — wrong shape.
Source belongs on master alongside the lib it documents, and the
multiplexer publishes built artifacts to gh-pages.

- showcase/ — Vite + React app consuming showcase-kit's components.
  Page is composed (not templated) from <Header>, <ScrollPin>,
  <CodeBlock>, <MetadataFooter>. The debugging demo is a full React
  port of the previous vanilla orchestrator (useReducer + cancellable
  async play loop, scenarios as typed data).
- .github/workflows/pages-deploy.yml — adapted from the shader-playground
  pattern: trigger on master push + PRs, compute a slot name
  (r<count>-<sha> for master, pr-N for PRs, tag name for tags), build
  Vite with VITE_BASE pointing at /electric-cherry/<slot>/, hand the
  built dist to brandon-fryslie/gh-pages-multiplexer@v1 with
  base-path-mode: none (Vite already produced the right base).

Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.ai/code)
via [Happy](https://happy.engineering)

Co-Authored-By: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>
Co-Authored-By: Happy <yesreply@happy.engineering>

Extract MCP tool catalog; showcase reads it as single source of truth

Two coupled changes:

1. Move the inline `tools: Tool[]` array out of src/index.ts into a new
   src/tool-catalog.ts. The catalog file has zero runtime dependencies
   (locally-defined types, no SDK imports) so a browser bundle can
   import it as readily as the Node MCP server. Each entry now carries
   a `category` field so consumers can group without re-deriving the
   taxonomy from name patterns.

2. Replace the showcase demo's clickable-chip behavior. Old behavior
   pushed a synthetic round-trip through the wire log — informative
   only insofar as the chip felt alive. New behavior opens a modal
   "tool inspector" populated entirely from TOOL_CATALOG: description,
   typed parameter list with required/default/enum metadata, and an
   example call synthesized from the schema's required fields. The
   showcase no longer ships hand-written examples that drift; the
   inspector renders whatever the server's schema currently says.

   Showcase's data/tools.ts also derives palette grouping from the
   catalog's `category` field. The palette layout, group labels, and
   protocol routing per group are all generated from one pass through
   TOOL_CATALOG. The hardcoded TOOL_PALETTE / GROUP_LABEL /
   GROUP_PROTOCOL maps are gone — adding a tool to the catalog with a
   known category makes it appear in the palette automatically. Tool
   count in the palette header now derives from TOOL_CATALOG.length.

The dataflow particle layer is removed entirely (DataflowLayer.tsx
deleted, flowPackets state torn out of usePlayer). The user's feedback
was that the animation wasn't useful — info is. The palette now
behaves as an interactive reference card for the live MCP catalog.

Showcase tsconfig adds ../src/tool-catalog.ts to its include list, and
the Vite config opens server.fs.allow to '..' so the dev server can
read the catalog file. Production builds aren't restricted by fs.allow.

Demo: clickable tool chips + dataflow particles between panels

Two related changes:

1. Tool chips in the palette are now buttons. Clicking one fires off a
   one-shot manual invocation: highlights the chip, emits a wire row
   round-trip on the chip's protocol (CDP or V8), and shows the same
   dataflow animation a scripted scenario does. Doesn't disrupt the
   running scenario — visitors get tactile feedback that the chips are
   real entry points and which protocol each routes to.

2. New `<DataflowLayer>` overlays the stage and animates SVG particles
   along curved paths between source/target rects (chip ↔ application
   pane) for every wire-message round-trip. Each particle is a row in
   `state.flowPackets` with `protocol` and source/target selectors —
   the orchestrator appends, the layer renders, each <Packet>
   self-removes via timer when its animateMotion completes. No
   choreography in user code; it's all driven by state.

Selectors live in the packet so the layer has no domain knowledge of
"which side does what" — only the orchestrator decides chip→app vs
app→chip per direction.
